studies.title: More dozens sold; lower prices and margins
studies.whyHere: Volume / price divergence and margin compression; not verified pipeline selection.
studies.timingNote: Printed publication date only; exact intraday dissemination is unverified.
studies.finding: Reported volume growth coexisted with lower realized prices, sales and gross margin. Volume alone would have missed deterioration; this is a retained counterexample to a simple growth narrative.
studies.businessQuestion: Does a matched volume/price decomposition improve next-reported-quarter gross-margin forecasts beyond last reported margin? Freeze a dated sample and rule before examining outcomes.
studies.falsifier: Reject added predictive value if the decomposition does not beat the same-date persistence baseline out of sample; record all negative cases.
studies.nextAction: Obtain independently timed additional filings and outcome labels; preserve fiscal periods, egg-product mix, inventory and purchases before testing. No forecast or market-return test has run.
limitations: Archived 2024 example, not a current company assessment or buy signal.
Pipeline recurrence and first appearance are unknown; repeated mentions are not independent confirmations.
One source vintage supplies both comparative columns, not two independent evidence events.
Sold and produced denominators differ; feed cost per produced dozen is not subtracted from selling price per sold dozen.
No cohort investment/payback, verified ROIC, forward valuation or shareholder-return result is supplied.
Publication is date-only; not eligible for an intraday historical signal test.

studies.title: Customer revenue fell despite a procurement-growth hypothesis
periods: FY2025 and FY2024 as reported in the FY2025 filing
studies.finding: HHS customer revenue declined in the retained annual disclosure. These labels can test a business-revenue hypothesis, but selected prime award obligations are not the same population as issuer revenue, which includes subcontract activity.
studies.whyHere: A negative customer-revenue case and a check on procurement-to-revenue assumptions, not a verified recurring pipeline lead.
studies.timingNote: SEC acceptance instants are retained. The earlier analysis's acceptance-plus-24-hour cutoff is a convention, not verified first public dissemination. FY2024 dollar revenue here is known from the FY2025 vintage, not retroactively from the FY2024 filing.
studies.businessQuestion: Does a complete, time-stamped customer award cohort improve next-year customer-revenue forecasts beyond the last disclosed annual revenue? Resolve prime/subcontract scope before testing.
studies.falsifier: Reject the procurement hypothesis if matched, then-public obligations fail to beat same-date revenue persistence, or if issuer/entity and revenue scopes cannot be reconciled.
studies.nextAction: Resolve historical parent/UEI ownership and obtain original transaction-publication vintages and a complete customer cohort; no return test is justified by these selected labels.
limitations: The three dollar observations are comparative columns from one later filing, not three contemporaneously available vintages.
Two inspected filings are not two independent confirmations or a complete history.
Current cumulative award amounts are not revenue or period obligation flows; parent identity and disclosure scope remain blockers.
Rounded annual revenue labels and unknown transaction first-public times do not support an intraday event backtest.
No reinvestment payback, current valuation or stock-return evidence is supplied.

studies.title: Operational recovery is not automatically business growth

source.title: Issuer furnished production update in February 2025 filing

periods: September 2024 closure disclosure through February 2025 production disclosure
studies.finding: The selected disclosures progress from closure to partial restart to reported pre-hurricane production. This is a positive operational recovery case, not evidence of incremental growth, full supply restoration or profitable shareholder returns.
studies.whyHere: A contrasting recovery case. Three filings about one episode do not constitute independent confirmations or genuine pipeline recurrence.
studies.timingNote: The retained SEC metadata binds acceptance times to accessions. Original exhibit bytes and earliest public dissemination were not archived. The November update describes an already-announced restart; do not date the first physical restart from its filename or filing date.
studies.businessQuestion: Can source-timed changes in a disclosed recovery expectation improve an operational-state forecast beyond the last known state? First distinguish production, shipment and allocation normalization.
studies.falsifier: Reject added value if the dated expectation adds nothing beyond last reported state; exclude earnings-bundled price reactions until confounders and exposure are resolved.
studies.nextAction: Find earlier original dissemination vintages and comparable independent episodes; reconcile facility/product ownership and revenue exposure before any business-growth or market-return test.
limitations: One selected episode, not a representative outage cohort.
Two disclosures are earnings-bundled; restart information was already public before the November filing.
SEC metadata verifies filing timestamps, not every content claim in a furnished exhibit.
Production recovery does not prove shipments or normalized customer allocations.
The January 2025 Kidney Care sale is an ownership/exposure confound; no automatic plant-to-revenue mapping.
No current valuation, incremental capital return or stock-return evidence is supplied.

selectionRule: Reuse the existing egg/accounting, procurement and facility-recovery tracks; retain negative and recovery cases, without selecting on subsequent stock returns. This is convenience coverage, not a frozen historical cohort.
